install_startup.recipe_modification_note: No Dockerfile/compose file in the repo and no official Docker Hub image - a plain Laravel 12 app meant to be deployed onto an existing PHP/webserver stack. Wrote a Dockerfile.library (Ubuntu 24.04 base, not the official Debian-based php Docker Hub image - this sandbox's egress policy denies all Debian apt mirrors including deb.debian.org, while Ubuntu's own default mirrors are allowed and Ubuntu 24.04 already ships PHP 8.3). Ubuntu's default apt sources use plain HTTP, which this sandbox's proxy rejects with 405 (it only tunnels HTTPS) - switched them to https:// and bootstrapped apt's trust store directly from the proxy's CA bundle before the first apt-get update (the base image ships no ca-certificates package yet, and apt won't fetch one without HTTPS trust first - chicken-and-egg, solved by writing the bundle straight to /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt and /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ so the real ca-certificates package's install doesn't wipe it). A handful of composer dependencies (myclabs/deep-copy, webklex/laravel-imap, prettus/l5-repository, smalot/pdfparser, mpdf/mpdf, ...) have no Packagist-hosted dist zip and fall back to GitHub's codeload API, which hit an exhausted 60/hour anonymous rate limit from repeated use earlier in this pipeline session - the repo's own composer.json forces 'preferred-install: dist', which disables Composer's automatic git-source fallback; overriding with `composer install --prefer-source` uses git clone for every package instead (this sandbox's proxy does inject real GitHub credentials for git operations specifically), avoiding the anonymous API limit entirely. MySQL (mysql:8.4) via a standard compose service. Ran the project's own installer (`php artisan krayin-crm:install --skip-env-check --no-interaction`), which creates a default admin (admin@example.com/admin123) since its account-creation prompts have defaults and --no-interaction accepts them; the admin's own account-settings page was then used to reset the email/password to the pipeline's standard libwalker/Walker-Pass-2026! test credentials, letting the standard screens.py crawler log in and complete a real 15-screen walkthrough on its own (9 fully rendered - CRM detail views for a fresh install with no seed data render a loading-skeleton state, which is genuine app behavior, not a crawler failure).
